sections.h2: Where is Conway, SC, and how big is it?
sections.html:
Conway is the county seat of Horry County, on the western bank of the Waccamaw River on the South Carolina Coastal Plain. It lies about 14 miles from the Atlantic Ocean and is part of the Myrtle Beach metro area.

The city is small in area but has grown quickly. The 2020 census counted 24,849 residents, up 45.3 percent from 17,103 in 2010, and the 2025 estimate is 30,627.

sections.h2: How did Conway get its name and its start?
sections.html:
The town was founded in 1732 under Royal Governor Robert Johnson's Township Scheme, on a bluff above the Waccamaw. Colonists called it Kings Town, and the name later became Kingston. Horry County was created in 1801 with its courthouse in Kingston.

The name then changed to Conwayborough, honoring General Robert Conway, and in 1883 the General Assembly renamed it Conway. A river town with that history has older blocks near downtown and newer subdivisions farther out, and the two sell differently.

Downtown revitalization began with the Main Street USA project in the 1980s, and the Riverwalk along the Waccamaw is now a restaurant district. Houses within walking distance of it are the ones sellers tend to mention first.

sections.h2: What jobs and schools anchor Conway's housing market?
sections.html:
Conway's anchors are Coastal Carolina University, county government and a handful of industrial employers. Named employers include New South Companies (a Canfor subsidiary), Vulcan Materials Company and AVX Corporation.

The Grainger Generating Station, a Santee Cooper coal plant, ran from 1966 until it retired in 2012. Horry-Georgetown Technical College and a Webster University branch also operate in the area, and most of the county is served by Horry County Schools.

Coastal Carolina University also runs the 3,370-seat HTC Center on its campus. Proximity to the university is a useful fact to mention in any listing or cash offer discussion.

sections.h2: How bad is flooding in Conway, and how does it affect a sale?
sections.html:
Flooding is the main risk factor for houses near the Waccamaw River, and Hurricane Florence set the record. The National Weather Service reports the river at Conway crested at a record 21.16 feet in 2018, breaking the Hurricane Matthew crest by more than three feet.

The Horry County emergency plan lists these Waccamaw flood stages:

  • Minor flooding at 11 feet, when roads may be covered.
  • Moderate flooding at 12 feet, when buildings usually begin to flood.
  • Major flooding at 14 to 16 feet, when large-scale evacuations may be needed.

The county plan also notes that the watershed is large and flat, so water can take days to reach the river and stay high for a long time. After Hurricane Florence, nearly 1,000 homes and businesses near the river flooded, and county officials later reported 361 damaged homes in Conway. After Hurricane Joaquin in 2015 and Hurricane Matthew in 2016, hundreds more homes in the county were damaged.

The City of Conway says its riverfront parks are designed to flood, which helps protect private property, and that it changed the electrical boxes in Riverfront Park so they can be removed ahead of rising water. If your house has flooded before, buyers will ask. Keep repair receipts, photos and any flood insurance claims together. See the NWS Hurricane Florence summary.

sections.h2: What is the climate in Conway, and what does it do to a house?
sections.html:
Conway has a humid subtropical climate with mild winters and hot, humid summers. The mean daily high is 58.1 degrees Fahrenheit in January and 90.8 in July, and August is the wettest month at 7.81 inches.

Heavy summer rain and a high water table are hard on crawl spaces, drainage and roofs. Buyers' inspectors in Conway look for moisture, so a dry crawl space and clean gutters help a house show better.

The city runs under a mayor-council system with a mayor and six at-large council members serving staggered four-year terms. The council meets on the first and third Mondays at 4 p.m., and that is where zoning and annexation questions end up.

sections.h2: What roads and transit connect Conway to the rest of the region?
sections.html:
U.S. Routes 501 and 378 pass through Conway, and the Conway-Horry County Airport (HYW) is about 4 miles west of town on US 378. Coast RTA serves much of the county, with its main station downtown, and the R.J. Corman Carolina Line short-line railroad runs through the city.

Florence closed more than 260 roads in Horry County, so access in a storm is part of how buyers judge a Conway address. A house on higher ground with a clear route out is easier to show than one on a street that floods.

sections.h2: How does property tax work for a Conway house?
sections.html:
Horry County assesses property in Conway, and South Carolina taxes an owner-occupied legal residence at 4 percent of fair market value, versus 6 percent for other property. The residence and up to five contiguous acres qualify, and the house cannot be rented for more than 72 days in a calendar year. The owner must apply before the first penalty date for the year in which eligibility is first claimed (Code section 12-43-220).

A buyer who rents the house out will not get the 4 percent rate, so the bill after a sale to an investor can be higher than yours. The county Assessor's Office is at 1301 Second Avenue, Conway, SC 29526, open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., phone (843) 915-5040. Its Land Records application finds a parcel's PIN by address or owner name, and the PIN is needed for the county Tax Estimator. See the Assessor page. We could not confirm the reassessment year or appeal dates on that page, so ask the office.

sections.h2: What happens with an inherited house in Conway?
sections.html:
A deed that distributes an estate does not need the usual value affidavit under South Carolina Code section 12-24-70(D), which makes the paperwork lighter than for an ordinary sale. A deed to a mortgagee in lieu of foreclosure is also exempt from the deed recording fee under section 12-24-40.

The heirs still have to agree, and the house still needs a clear title. Horry County records are in the county, so a closing attorney will pull the chain of title before anything is signed.

Common situations for Conway sellers include:

  • A house flooded in a past storm that needs repairs before a bank will lend.
  • A rental with a tenant and no plan to repair.
  • An inherited house with several heirs in different states.
  • A home with mortgage arrears and a deadline.

faqs.q: How much did the Waccamaw River rise in Hurricane Florence?
faqs.a: The National Weather Service reports a record crest of 21.16 feet at Conway, more than three feet above the Hurricane Matthew crest. Nearly 1,000 homes and businesses near the river flooded.

faqs.q: What is the 4 percent rate on a Conway house?
faqs.a: It is the assessment ratio for an owner-occupied legal residence in South Carolina, compared with 6 percent for other property. The home cannot be rented for more than 72 days a year, and you must apply before the first penalty date.

faqs.q: Where do I find a parcel's PIN in Horry County?
faqs.a: Use the county's Land Records application at horrycountysc.gov, which finds a PIN by address or owner name. The Assessor's Office at (843) 915-5040 can help.

faqs.q: Is a flooded Conway house hard to sell?
faqs.a: It can be, since buyers and lenders ask about flood history and insurance. Keep repair records and your flood zone information handy, and ask for a cash offer if repairs are not an option.

faqs.q: Does Conway have its own city services?
faqs.a: Yes. The city lists 14 departments, including Planning and Development, Public Utilities, Solid Waste and Construction Services. Use those offices for permits and utility transfers when you sell.
